newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Renewed positive sentiment saw South African bond yields end below the 15.30 percent level and dealers said the market could re-enter a bull channel if it broke below 15.27 percent at the start of next week.

Sentiment turned rosier after local institutions returned to the market at the higher levels on Thursday and on news of a shortlist of candidates to take up to a 30 percent equity stake in state telecommunications utility Telkom, traders said.
At 1420 GMT the benchmark R150 bond yield was hovering at the key 15.27 percent level from 15.375 percent late on Thursday.
The yield broke through 15.30 percent in the afternoon in line with the U.S. market which reacted favourably to the release of U.S producer price and retail sales data.
"The guys were looking for something to test the lower levels and the U.S data provided the impetus, ensuring a bullish close," a senior bond trader said.
But he noted that the rand had broken significant levels on the upside on Thursday and there was a lot of nervousness about the currency's next moves.
"The market will take direction from the rand and U.S. rates at the start of next week in the absence of fresh economic data," the dealer added.
Traders said local institutions had been scarce and trade had been mostly jobber-driven with some demand from offshore.
Bond Exchange figures show foreigners sold a net 87.16 million rand of South African bonds on Thursday after buying a net 74.55 million rand of bonds on Wednesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes amounted to 35.82 billion rand on Thursday, a settlement date, from 3.06 billion rand on Wednesday.
The rand ended a slow day just over a cent stronger after it took a hammering on Thursday, sinking to its lowest level in seven weeks.
"Volumes were small and it was a dull day compared to Thursday's activity," a dealer said, adding that the unit had benefited from London-based dollar sales.
Another dealer said attempts by London players to push the rand below the 4.54 level on the downside were met by dollar demand.
"The upside remains the scary side and while there was some reprieve today (Friday) it looks like we could test the higher 4.56 level again next week," he added.
At 1412 GMT the rand was trading at 4.5410/5460 on a stronger U.S. dollar from 4.5515/5565 overnight.
Against the crosses the rand was last trading at an all-time low of 7.1529/1653 on sterling from 7.1258/1382 on Thursday and at 0.3367/3372 marks from 0.3355/3361 marks previously.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.75 and 15.95 percent, while 90-day BAs were also unchanged at between 15.20 and 15.40 percent.
The daily shortage was quoted at 7.432 billion rand on Thursday from 7.749 billion rand on Wednesday.
